title: Ray Nance's early violin sextet in Chicago
summary: Ray Nance was a Chicago star leading a six-piece band with three doubling violinists before joining Duke.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: But you knew Ray before he went with Duke, didn't you? Or did you know of him?

I knew him, yeah. But I -- you know, in those days Ray Nance was one of the Chicago stars, if you want to put it that way. Even though he didn't act like it. He was never arrogant. But Ray was one of the -- he had one of the nicest little six pieces, you know. All three of them in the front line played violin.
They doubled. Just like he did, you know?
Oh, I didn't realize what the instrumentation was. I knew he had a group. Didn't he start it when he was still in high school?
And I used to see some church programs where they would say Raymond Nance on violin. And he would play like church affairs and things like that.
Do you know who the musicians were that were in the front line in his band?
Oh, boy, let me see. John Levy would know. I know Spencer Odum (PHONETIC), who's passed, too. Used to play with the Southernairs, the quartet that used to come
And -- now I can't think of the rest of them, but John Levy would know, because he was coming along at that time, too, you know?
